text: SVG refraction through backdrop-filter: url(#filter) renders only in Chromium; Safari and Firefox need a different path (filter on the element's own pixels, a mirror copy, or a blur-only fallback).
note: Seven independent orgs state it in their own docs or code gates. No browser was run in this research step.

text: A portable refraction path exists: apply filter: url(#id) to the element's own content (or a copy of a known backdrop) instead of backdrop-filter, which renders in all three engines.
note: anubhavaanand, gentpan and jpoindexter all credit the same upstream (Aave Labs 'Building Glass for the Web'), which was not fetched; xenitV1 reaches the same result with a mirror copy.

text: Headless or software-rendered Chromium under-renders backdrop blur of 20px or more, so headless screenshots should not be used to tune large glass.
note: Single org (Tsdsj). gentpan documents different headless pitfalls (virtual time freezes springs, headless Firefox blanks WebGL), which does not confirm this one.

text: Displacement maps use 128 as the neutral channel value with offset = (C/255 - 0.5) * scale, and the filter needs color-interpolation-filters='sRGB' or the neutral point shifts.
note: Zettersten states the formula and the sRGB rule; gentpan lists sRGB among its engine-breaking rules; Tsdsj sets sRGB in code; Ashkanian uses the same 128+127*v/M encoding; anubhavaanand omits sRGB and the inspector flagged that as a likely bug.
